record.original_question: Can the Penrose inequality relating the area of an apparent horizon to the ADM mass be proved in the general case, or can one construct a genuine counterexample showing that the expected lower bound fails?

evidence.quote: Problem P3: Find a proof of the Penrose inequality or present a counterex￰ample in the general case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $(M,g,k)$ be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations, that is, a complete 3-manifold $M$ with Riemannian metric $g$ and symmetric (0,2)-tensor $k$ (the second fundamental form of an embedding into a spacetime), such that outside a compact set $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus B$ and in the asymptotic coordinates
$$g_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1}),\qquad \partial g_{ij} = O(|x|^{-2}),\qquad k_{ij} = O(|x|^{-2}),\qquad \partial k_{ij} = O(|x|^{-3}),$$
with the usual decay of scalar curvature and of $\mathrm{div}(k)-d(\mathrm{tr}\,k)$ ensuring a well-defined ADM mass
$$m_{\mathrm{ADM}} = \frac{1}{16\pi}\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}\!\bigl(\partial_j g_{ij}-\partial_i g_{jj}\bigr)\,\nu^i\,dA.$$
Assume the dominant energy condition
$$\mu \ge |J|_g, \qquad \mu := \tfrac12\bigl(R_g+(\mathrm{tr}_g k)^2-|k|_g^2\bigr),\quad J := \mathrm{div}_g(k-(\mathrm{tr}_g k)g).$$
Let $\Sigma \subset M$ be an outermost apparent horizon, i.e. an outermost closed 2-surface satisfying $H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma k = 0$ (future trapped) or $H_\Sigma - \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma k = 0$ (past trapped), and let $A$ denote its area.

Problem. Either prove the Penrose inequality
$$m_{\mathrm{ADM}} \;\ge\; \sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}}$$
in this general (non–time-symmetric) setting, or construct an asymptotically flat initial data set $(M,g,k)$ satisfying the dominant energy condition and containing an outermost apparent horizon for which the inequality fails.
artifact.status_search_result: The time-symmetric (Riemannian) Penrose inequality was proved by Huisken–Ilmanen (single horizon, 2001) and Bray (multiple horizons, 2001). The general non–time-symmetric (full spacetime) Penrose inequality remains open. Recent work in 2024–2025 has produced unconditional spacetime Penrose-type inequalities with universally valid but non-sharp lower bounds, and Penrose-type inequalities under additional hypotheses (static, integral energy conditions, matter density), but the sharp general conjecture with full rigidity is not resolved.

status_evidence.snippet: Proving the general Penrose inequality remains an open problem in general relativity, called the Penrose conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: General Penrose inequality remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Unconditional Spacetime Penrose Inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Major advances have been the establishment of unconditional Penrose-type inequalities... as achieved in April 2025 and May 2025.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) progress gives unconditional but suboptimal spacetime Penrose-type inequalities.

status_evidence.title: Present status of the Penrose inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the status of the Penrose inequality, with the Riemannian case proved and the general case open.
status_evidence.claim: The general case is open while the Riemannian case is proved.

status_evidence.title: A Penrose-Type Inequality for Static Spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Penrose-type inequality established in the static spacetime setting (2025).
status_evidence.claim: Special cases continue to be resolved while the general inequality is not.
